subject: physics_2
question_text: What type of transformer is used in a 6 V bed lamp?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: a bed lamp runs at 6 V while the mains supply is far above 6 V, so the voltage must be reduced; reducing an a.c. voltage is exactly what a step-down transformer (Nₛ < Nₚ, so Vₛ < Vₚ) does. The mains value is deliberately not stated as one number — it differs by region.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Name the type
lines: A 6 V bed lamp uses a step-down transformer.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the type in the first line.
steps.why: The lamp needs only 6 V while the mains supply is at a much higher voltage, so the transformer must lower the voltage — that is a step-down transformer.
common_mistakes: Writing step-up. The mains voltage must come down to 6 V, not go up.

recall.must_convey: That a 6 V bed lamp uses a step-down transformer.

steps.memory_tip: 6 V is far below the mains voltage, so the transformer steps the voltage down.

steps.label: The reason
lines: The mains supply is at a much higher voltage
than 6 V, so the voltage must be reduced.
A step-down transformer has fewer turns on
the secondary than on the primary, so Vₛ < Vₚ.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say why the voltage must come down and which coil has fewer turns.
steps.why: Naming the type earns the first mark; saying how a step-down transformer lowers the voltage — fewer secondary turns, so Vₛ < Vₚ — is what shows the physics rather than a memorised word.
common_mistakes: Saying a step-down transformer has fewer turns on the primary. The secondary has the fewer turns.

recall.must_convey: That the mains voltage must be reduced to 6 V, and a step-down transformer has fewer secondary turns so Vₛ < Vₚ.
accept: V s less than V p

steps.memory_tip: Step-down: voltage down, secondary turns down — both fall together.

insider_note: A one-word answer loses the second mark — say why the voltage must come down and which coil has fewer turns.
